column1: # Schema manifest: the order in which the files of this folder are applied to the core databases.
# Rows are applied one by one, top to bottom. A new .sql file in this folder needs a row here.
# Columns, separated by one tab. No field is empty: "-" stands for "none" (a shell `read` with a tab separator would
# merge two tabs and shift the columns).
#   db       cluster (roles, run in the `postgres` database) | memory_control | memory_open | memory_closed | memory_audit
#   file     a file of this folder
#   phase    fresh  — creates the base objects of a database; applied once, in one transaction, only while its marker
#                     object does not exist yet. A fresh file never runs on a database that already has data.
#            always — re-runnable on a database with data; applied on every run (install and upgrade).
#   marker   fresh rows: role:<name> or table:<name>, an object the file creates; always rows: -
#   vars     psql variables passed with -v, comma-separated: name=value is fixed, a bare name is supplied by the executor
#            (instance — the instance id, instance_name — its display name); - = none
#   profile  - = every installation; otherwise the name of the only install profile that applies the row
# Order: rows are applied strictly top to bottom, also across databases. Rows of the cluster come first. Roles belong
# to the whole cluster: the memory_control rows before the seed create roles (09-external-access.sql) that rows of
# other databases grant to (11-edge-export-records.sql, 13-edge-audit.sql), so a row whose file creates a role comes
# before every row of another database. Inside a database its fresh rows come before its always rows.
